source_meta._title: Clicking a settings button when there's a slider under the mouse in the next screen plays the click sound twice

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition client running the first listed affected version, Minecraft 19w11a. Use desktop mouse input and the title-screen menus; no world, server, commands, cheats, seed, or multiplayer connection is required. Game audio must be routed to an audible output device.
preconditions: Launch a vanilla, unmodified Minecraft Java Edition client so that mods do not change menu behavior or GUI sounds.
Use Minecraft 19w11a, the first version listed as affected. Do not use fix version 22w42a for this reproduction.
Ensure the operating system output device is unmuted and set to an audible level.
Ensure Minecraft's Master Volume is above 0%. If volume must be configured first, finish that configuration and return to the title screen before beginning the numbered procedure.
Use a physical mouse or an input device capable of keeping the left mouse button continuously depressed while the pointer is moved.
Begin on the fully loaded Minecraft title screen with the Options... button visible.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select the Java Edition installation configured for Minecraft 19w11a and start the game.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft 19w11a client window opens.

steps.action: Wait for startup to finish. Do not continue while the loading screen is displayed or the client window is unresponsive.
steps.success_cue: The title screen is fully rendered, accepts mouse movement, and shows the Options... button.

steps.action: Move the mouse pointer onto the center of the Options... button on the title screen. Do not press the mouse button yet.
steps.success_cue: The pointer is inside the Options... button and the button is visibly hovered.

steps.action: Press the left mouse button while the pointer is on Options..., and keep the physical mouse button continuously held down. Do not release it when the Options screen opens.
steps.exact_input: Left mouse button down; continue holding
steps.success_cue: The Options screen is visible while the left mouse button remains physically depressed.

steps.action: Without releasing the left mouse button, move the pointer upward from its current position and place it inside the rectangular FOV slider at the top of the Options screen. Target the slider control itself rather than nearby text or empty background.
steps.exact_input: Move mouse while continuing to hold the left mouse button
steps.success_cue: The Options screen remains open, the left mouse button is still held, and the pointer is visibly positioned within the FOV slider's bounds.

steps.action: With the pointer still positioned over the FOV slider, release the left mouse button once. Do not click again or move into another menu before handing off to observation.
steps.success_cue: The left mouse button has just been released over the FOV slider, and the Options screen remains the active screen.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just released the continuously held left mouse button while the pointer is over the FOV slider on the Options screen. Begin audio/UI observation immediately, without performing another click.
uncertainties: The report does not provide a formal numbered Steps to Reproduce section; this plan uses the deterministic title-screen-to-FOV-slider procedure explicitly described in the report description and comments.

The operating system, window resolution, GUI Scale, and exact pixel coordinates are not specified. The executor must identify the destination slider by its FOV label rather than by fixed screen coordinates.
The report does not specify audio levels. Requiring an audible output device and Master Volume above 0% is a practical prerequisite for observing a sound-related issue.
The report states that the analogous cursor movement does not reproduce when entering Video Settings, so this plan deliberately uses the Options screen's FOV slider instead.

source_meta._title: Repeaters and comparators use wood sounds for placing/breaking despite being made mostly of stone

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition client running snapshot 16w44a in a vanilla single-player Creative-mode world. Use the default resource pack and functional audio output, preferably headphones or speakers in a quiet environment. No dedicated server, commands, seed, coordinates, or additional players are required.
preconditions: Create or select a launcher installation whose version is snapshot 16w44a, the first version in the report's Affects Versions field.
Ensure the operating system and Minecraft client are not muted and that the selected headphones or speakers are working.
Use the default Minecraft resource pack and disable any mod or resource pack that replaces block sounds.
Use a single-player world in Creative mode so a repeater and comparator can be obtained without unrelated crafting or resource gathering.
Locate a clear area containing the exposed top face of a solid full block, such as an ordinary grass, dirt, or stone ground block, on which redstone components can be placed.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or select an installation configured for snapshot 16w44a and start the game with that installation.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft 16w44a title screen is displayed and the client is responsive.

steps.action: From the title screen, open Singleplayer and create a new world. Set Game Mode to Creative before creating it. Leave the seed and other world-generation settings at their defaults because the report specifies none.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player has spawned in a Creative-mode world and can fly or open the Creative inventory.

steps.action: Wait for the initial terrain around the player to finish rendering before performing the sound test.
steps.success_cue: Nearby terrain is visible, movement responds normally, and no world-loading pause is occurring.

steps.action: Open the pause menu and configure sound so block interactions are clearly audible. Open Options, then Music & Sounds. Set Master Volume and the Blocks sound category above zero; a high value such as 100% is suitable. Reduce Music to 0% if necessary so it cannot mask the short placement and breaking sounds, then return to the world.
steps.exact_input: Esc -> Options -> Music & Sounds -> Master Volume: above 0% -> Blocks: above 0% -> Music: 0% -> Done
steps.success_cue: The game is unpaused, Minecraft audio is audible, and background music is not masking block sounds.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory using the inventory action, whose default key is E, and open the Search Items tab.
steps.success_cue: The Creative inventory is open and a searchable item list is visible.

steps.action: Click the Creative inventory search field, enter the search term "repeater", locate the repeater item, and place one repeater into an empty hotbar slot. The hotbar is the row of nine item slots at the bottom of the inventory and game screen.
steps.success_cue: A repeater icon is present in one of the nine hotbar slots.

steps.action: Clear the search field, enter the search term "comparator", locate the comparator item, and place one comparator into a different hotbar slot next to the repeater.
steps.success_cue: The hotbar contains both a repeater and a comparator in separate slots.

steps.action: Close the inventory using E or Esc and select the repeater's hotbar slot using its number key or the mouse wheel.
steps.exact_input: E, then the repeater slot's number key
steps.success_cue: The inventory is closed, the repeater's hotbar slot is highlighted, and a repeater is shown in the player's hand.

steps.action: Move to a quiet, clear area and aim the crosshair at the exposed top face of a solid full ground block. Do not aim at the side of the block or at tall grass, because the repeater must be placed on a suitable upper surface.
steps.success_cue: The crosshair is resting on an unobstructed horizontal block surface within placement range, with the repeater still selected.

steps.action: Pause briefly without placing anything, allowing any unrelated ambient or movement sound to finish before beginning the controlled interaction sequence.
steps.success_cue: The repeater remains selected, the target surface is unobstructed, and no immediately preceding player-generated sound is still playing.

steps.action: Place the repeater once on the targeted top surface using the Use Item/Place Block action, whose default input is right-click. Perform only one click so that the placement sound is isolated.
steps.success_cue: A repeater is visibly positioned on top of the targeted block.

steps.action: Remain still for approximately one second so the repeater's placement sound can finish before the next interaction. Keep the crosshair aimed directly at the placed repeater.
steps.success_cue: The repeater remains in place, the crosshair targets it, and enough time has passed to prevent the next sound from overlapping its placement sound.

steps.action: Break the placed repeater once using the Attack/Destroy action, whose default input is left-click. In Creative mode, a single click should remove it immediately. Ensure the crosshair targets the repeater rather than its supporting block.
steps.success_cue: The repeater has disappeared while the supporting ground block remains intact.

steps.action: Wait approximately one second for the repeater's breaking sound to finish, then select the comparator's hotbar slot using its number key or the mouse wheel.
steps.success_cue: The comparator's hotbar slot is highlighted, a comparator is shown in the player's hand, and the previous interaction sound has had time to finish.

steps.action: Aim at the same unobstructed top surface and place the comparator once using the Use Item/Place Block action, whose default input is right-click. Perform only one click.
steps.success_cue: A comparator is visibly positioned on top of the targeted block.

steps.action: Remain still for approximately one second so the comparator's placement sound can finish. Keep the crosshair aimed directly at the comparator.
steps.success_cue: The comparator remains in place, the crosshair targets it, and enough time has passed to prevent the next sound from overlapping its placement sound.

steps.action: Break the placed comparator once using the Attack/Destroy action, whose default input is left-click. Ensure the crosshair targets the comparator rather than the supporting block.
steps.success_cue: The comparator has disappeared while the supporting ground block remains intact; both component types have now each been placed and broken once.

stor.handoff_condition: Hand off to audio observation immediately before step 11, when the repeater is selected, the crosshair is aimed at a suitable solid top surface, audio is enabled, and the comparator is available in another hotbar slot. Continue observation through step 17 so the four isolated interactions—repeater placement, repeater breaking, comparator placement, and comparator breaking—are captured without overlapping player-generated sounds.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a game mode, world seed, coordinates, difficulty, or server environment. A new single-player Creative-mode world is selected as the simplest deterministic way to obtain and test the two components.

The report does not specify exact audio volume values or listening hardware. Audible Master and Blocks volume levels, optional headphones, and disabled background music are practical choices for isolating the interaction sounds.
The report lists many affected versions. Snapshot 16w44a is recommended solely because it is the first entry in the supplied Affects Versions field, as required by the version-selection policy.
Launcher and menu wording can vary by launcher release and operating system, but the required game version remains snapshot 16w44a.

source_meta._title: The "minecraft:item.bundle.remove_one" sound plays even when no items are unpacked from bundles

stor.environment: Unmodified Minecraft Java Edition 1.18 in a single-player world with commands enabled. Use a fresh Survival-mode world for a simple, standard player-inventory layout. Game and operating-system audio must be audible.
preconditions: Launch exactly Minecraft Java Edition 1.18, the first version listed as affected in the report; do not use fix version 24w33a.
Use a world in which cheats are enabled so the in-game /give command can be executed.
Use the standard player inventory interface, with at least one inventory or hotbar slot available for the bundle.
Do not place any items inside the bundle after obtaining it; the trigger requires the bundle to be empty.
Ensure Minecraft is not muted, the operating-system output device is audible, and relevant sound-volume sliders are above 0%.

Default controls are assumed: T opens chat, E opens the inventory, left-click picks up an item stack, and right-click performs the secondary inventory-slot action. If controls are rebound, use the bindings for those actions instead.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select and start an installation using Java Edition version 1.18. Wait for the main menu to finish loading.
steps.success_cue: The lower-left area of the main menu identifies the running game version as Minecraft 1.18.

steps.action: From the main menu, select Singleplayer, create a fresh world, set Game Mode to Survival, set Allow Cheats to ON, and create the world. Wait until terrain has rendered and player movement responds normally.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Survival -> Allow Cheats: ON -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in a loaded single-player world and commands are permitted.

steps.action: Confirm that sound can be heard. If necessary, press Esc, open Options and then Music & Sounds, set Master Volume above 0%, and make sure the operating-system audio output is not muted. Return to the world afterward.
steps.exact_input: Esc -> Options -> Music & Sounds -> Master Volume: above 0%
steps.success_cue: Minecraft and the operating-system audio output are unmuted, with Minecraft sound volume above 0%.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat. Type the report's command exactly, including the leading slash, and press Enter to execute it.
steps.success_cue: Command feedback reports that a bundle was given, and a bundle icon appears in an available hotbar or inventory slot.

steps.action: Press E to open the player inventory. Locate the newly granted bundle in the hotbar or main inventory grid. Do not put any items into it.
steps.success_cue: The player inventory is open, the empty bundle is visible in one of its slots, and at least one inventory slot is empty.

steps.action: Move the pointer over the bundle and left-click it once to pick it up from its slot, so the bundle stack is held by the mouse cursor rather than stored in a slot.
steps.success_cue: The bundle icon follows the mouse cursor, and the inventory slot from which it was picked up is now empty.

steps.action: Without left-clicking or placing the bundle, move the cursor over an empty slot in the player's inventory or hotbar. The now-empty source slot may be used as the target.
steps.exact_input: move cursor over an empty inventory slot
steps.success_cue: The empty bundle remains attached to the cursor, and the cursor is positioned over a slot containing no item.

steps.action: Right-click the empty inventory slot exactly once while continuing to hold the empty bundle on the cursor. Do not perform any additional inventory interactions after this click.
steps.success_cue: The secondary-click interaction has just been applied to an empty inventory slot while the empty bundle remains held by the cursor; the inventory is still open and the test is ready for immediate sound observation.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just right-clicked an empty inventory slot exactly once while holding a freshly granted, empty bundle on the mouse cursor. Keep the inventory open, make no further inputs, and immediately hand off to the observation subsystem to inspect the sound event produced by that single interaction.
uncertainties: The report does not specify single-player versus multiplayer or a game mode. A fresh single-player Survival world with cheats enabled is selected as the simplest deterministic environment with the standard player-inventory interface.
The report does not name a required sound-category slider. The plan therefore requires Minecraft audio generally to be unmuted rather than assigning the sound to an unverified category.

The formal reproduction step says to right-click while holding the bundle but does not explicitly name the target slot there. The report's accompanying code analysis specifies that the relevant interaction is right-clicking an empty inventory slot, so the execution plan uses that target.

source_meta._title: Equipping a player head, skull or carved pumpkin displays the generic "Gear equips" subtitle

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 1.19 Pre-release 1 in a new single-player Creative-mode world. Use the default integrated server. Enable subtitles and keep the Master Volume and Players sound-category volumes above 0%. Default controls are assumed: E for inventory, Esc for the pause menu, number keys for hotbar selection, and right-click for Use Item/Place Block.
preconditions: Launch the exact affected version, Minecraft Java Edition 1.19 Pre-release 1; do not use the fix version 1.19 Pre-release 2.
Use a newly created Creative-mode world so the comparison armor item and carved pumpkin can be obtained without crafting or commands.
The player's chest and head armor slots must be empty before the respective items are equipped.
Subtitles must be enabled through Options -> Music & Sounds -> Show Subtitles: ON.
Keep the Master Volume and Players sound-category sliders above 0% so equipment sound events are not suppressed.
Use an iron chestplate as the report's ordinary armor comparison item and a carved pumpkin as the report's head-slot test item.
Avoid other actions, entities, or environmental sources that produce sounds while performing the two equipment actions.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or select an installation that uses the exact version "1.19 Pre-release 1", launch it, and wait for the main menu to finish loading.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft main menu is responsive and identifies the running version as 1.19 Pre-release 1.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, choose Create New World, set Game Mode to Creative, and create the world. No particular seed is required. Wait after spawning until nearby terrain has rendered and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in a loaded single-player world in Creative mode and can move normally.

steps.action: Press Esc, open Options, then Music & Sounds. Set Show Subtitles to ON. Also ensure that Master Volume and the Players sound-category volume are above 0%, then select Done until gameplay resumes.
steps.success_cue: Gameplay has resumed with Show Subtitles enabled and the relevant sound-volume controls set above 0%.

steps.action: Press E to open the Creative inventory, open the Search Items tab, activate the search field, and search for an iron chestplate.
steps.success_cue: An iron chestplate is visible among the Creative inventory search results.

steps.action: Move one iron chestplate from the search results into hotbar slot 1. The hotbar is the row of nine item slots at the bottom of the inventory screen.
steps.success_cue: Hotbar slot 1 contains one iron chestplate.

steps.action: Clear the Creative inventory search field and search for a carved pumpkin.
steps.success_cue: A carved pumpkin is visible among the Creative inventory search results.

steps.action: Move one carved pumpkin from the search results into hotbar slot 2, then press E to close the inventory and return to gameplay.
steps.success_cue: Hotbar slot 1 contains the iron chestplate, hotbar slot 2 contains the carved pumpkin, and no inventory or pause menu is open.

steps.action: Press 1, or otherwise select hotbar slot 1, to place the iron chestplate in the active hotbar slot.
steps.success_cue: The iron chestplate is visibly held by the player and its hotbar slot is highlighted.

steps.action: Aim the crosshair into unobstructed open air rather than at an interactive block or entity, then right-click once to use and equip the iron chestplate. Do not perform another action immediately afterward.
steps.success_cue: The iron chestplate is no longer held in the active hotbar slot, indicating that it has moved into the empty chest armor slot.

steps.action: Wait without moving, opening a menu, changing items, or producing additional sounds until the temporary subtitle generated by the chestplate-equipping action is no longer displayed.
steps.success_cue: The subtitle display area is clear and ready for the separate carved-pumpkin equipment event.

steps.action: Press 2, or otherwise select hotbar slot 2, to place the carved pumpkin in the active hotbar slot. Aim into unobstructed open air, preferably upward into the sky, so the carved pumpkin will not be placed as a block.
steps.success_cue: The carved pumpkin is visibly held, its hotbar slot is highlighted, and the crosshair is not targeting a surface on which it could be placed.

steps.action: Right-click exactly once to use and equip the carved pumpkin in the empty head armor slot. Do not open a menu, change items, move, or produce another sound after this input; immediately hand control to the observation subsystem.
steps.success_cue: The equipment input has just completed and the carved-pumpkin first-person overlay confirms that the pumpkin is being worn.

stor.handoff_condition: The carved pumpkin has just been equipped in the player's head armor slot with subtitles enabled, after the earlier iron-chestplate equipment subtitle was allowed to clear. Begin observing the subtitle generated by this single equipment event before it disappears.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a game mode, world seed, coordinates, or multiplayer requirement. A new single-player Creative-mode world is selected as the simplest deterministic way to obtain the required items.

The report allows any armor piece or elytra for the comparison action and any head or carved pumpkin for the test action. This plan selects an iron chestplate and carved pumpkin as concrete representative items without changing the reported reproduction logic.

The report does not specify whether equipment is moved through the inventory or equipped with the Use Item control. This plan uses one right-click in open air for each item as a practical, repeatable equipment method.
The exact volume levels are not provided by the report. Nonzero Master Volume and Players volume are used only to avoid suppressing the equipment sound events involved in the subtitle test.
Default key bindings are assumed. If controls are rebound, use the bindings assigned to Inventory, Pause Menu, Hotbar Slot 1, Hotbar Slot 2, and Use Item/Place Block.

source_meta._title: Subtitles string "subtitles.block.trial_spawner.spawn_mob" is misleading and inconsistent

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition, single-player integrated world, version 23w45a, English (US) language, Update 1.21 experimental features enabled, Creative mode used only to construct and configure the test fixture, Survival mode used for the trigger, and subtitles enabled. Use an unmodified client without resource packs that replace English language strings.
preconditions: The Minecraft Launcher must be able to install and launch the historical Java Edition snapshot 23w45a.
Use a new disposable test world rather than an important existing world because 23w45a is a snapshot and the Update 1.21 experiment marks the world as experimental.
Use the vanilla English (US) language resources; disable resource packs that alter translations or subtitle text.

The report supplies no seed, coordinates, world type, difficulty, or required Trial Spawner mob. This plan uses a Superflat world and a Zombie Spawn Egg to produce the reported Trial Spawner spawn event deterministically.

Default controls are assumed: E opens the inventory, Esc opens the pause menu, T opens chat, number keys select hotbar slots, W moves forward, and right-click uses or places the selected item. Use the equivalent bound controls if these have been changed.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, open Installations, enable access to snapshots if necessary, create or edit an installation, select historical version 23w45a, and launch it.
steps.success_cue: The Java Edition title screen is open and identifies the running version as 23w45a.

steps.action: From the title screen, open Options, then Language, and select English (US). Confirm the selection and return to the title screen.
steps.success_cue: The menus are displayed using English (US).

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, then Create New World. Enter a recognizable disposable world name.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World screen is open with the test-world name entered.

steps.action: On the Create New World screen, open More, select Experiments, turn on the Update 1.21 experiment, confirm any experimental-feature warning, and return to the world-creation screen.
steps.success_cue: The Update 1.21 experiment is enabled for the new world.

steps.action: On the Game tab, set Game Mode to Creative and set Difficulty to Easy. Creative mode is only being used to obtain and configure the Trial Spawner; the actual trigger will occur after changing to Survival mode.
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen shows Creative mode and Easy difficulty.

steps.action: Open the World tab and set World Type to Superflat so the Trial Spawner will have a level, unobstructed spawning area.
steps.success_cue: The selected world type is Superflat.

steps.action: Select Create New World, accept the experimental-world confirmation if it appears, and wait for world generation and chunk loading to finish.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in the new world, nearby terrain is rendered, and movement responds normally.

steps.action: Press Esc, select Options, then Accessibility Settings, set Show Subtitles to ON, and use Done until gameplay resumes.
steps.success_cue: Gameplay has resumed with the Show Subtitles accessibility option enabled.

steps.action: Move to an open patch of level ground with several unobstructed blocks on every side. Avoid placing the test fixture immediately beside a village building, animal pen, or other source of frequent unrelated sounds.
steps.success_cue: There is a clear, level area around the intended placement position, with enough open floor for a mob to appear near the Trial Spawner.

steps.action: Press E to open the Creative inventory. Open the Search Items tab, search for Trial Spawner, and place one Trial Spawner item into an empty hotbar slot. Then replace the search text with Zombie Spawn Egg and place one Zombie Spawn Egg into another hotbar slot.
steps.success_cue: The hotbar contains both a Trial Spawner and a Zombie Spawn Egg.

steps.action: Close the inventory with E. Select the hotbar slot containing the Trial Spawner, aim at the top surface of the ground near the center of the open area, and right-click once to place it.
steps.success_cue: One Trial Spawner block is placed on the ground with open floor around it.

steps.action: Select the Zombie Spawn Egg in the hotbar, aim directly at the placed Trial Spawner, and right-click the Trial Spawner once. Do not right-click an adjacent ground block. A Creative-placed Trial Spawner initially has no mob type, and using a spawn egg on it configures its mob type.
steps.success_cue: The Trial Spawner is configured for zombies; its internal mob display indicates a zombie rather than remaining unconfigured.

steps.action: While still in Creative mode, move at least 20 blocks horizontally away from the Trial Spawner so that changing game mode will not activate it prematurely. Keep the block within view or record its direction before moving.
steps.exact_input: At least 20 blocks of horizontal separation
steps.success_cue: The Trial Spawner remains located and loaded, but the player is well away from it.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat, type the exact game-mode command including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The command succeeds, the Creative inventory is no longer available, and the normal Survival health and hunger bars are visible.

steps.action: Face the Trial Spawner and walk toward it using the forward movement control, W by default. Continue until the Trial Spawner notices the Survival player and begins its activation sequence, then stop moving.
steps.success_cue: The player remains in Survival mode near the Trial Spawner, and the block has entered its active state with its activation animation or particles visible.

steps.action: Stand a few blocks from the active Trial Spawner, keep the camera aimed toward the block and its surrounding spawn area, and leave the subtitle overlay area on the right side of the screen unobstructed by menus. Do not attack the spawner or leave its vicinity.
steps.success_cue: The active Trial Spawner and its nearby open spawning area are visible while subtitles remain enabled.

steps.action: Remain beside the active Trial Spawner and wait only until it completes its first mob-spawning action. Do not attack the spawned mob before handing control to the observation subsystem.
steps.success_cue: A zombie spawned by the Trial Spawner has just materialized near the block.

stor.handoff_condition: The player is in Survival mode beside the configured and active Trial Spawner, subtitles remain enabled, and the Trial Spawner has just spawned its first zombie. Begin observing the subtitle produced by that spawn event immediately, before performing any further action.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a seed, coordinates, world type, difficulty, or mob type. Superflat terrain, Easy difficulty, and a zombie were selected as practical deterministic setup choices and are not claimed as bug requirements.

The report instructs the player to stand next to a Trial Spawner but does not require a naturally generated Trial Chamber. This plan uses a Creative-placed Trial Spawner configured with a Zombie Spawn Egg, then changes the player to Survival before activation. Official version information confirms that Creative-placed Trial Spawners can be configured with spawn eggs and that Creative players are not detected by them.
Trial Spawners were experimental in 23w45a, so the Update 1.21 experiment must be enabled when creating the world. Experimental features cannot normally be enabled afterward for an existing world.

The report comment provides `/tellraw @s {"translate":"subtitles.block.trial_spawner.spawn_mob"}` as an alternative way to inspect the translation string. The primary plan does not use that shortcut because it would display translated text in chat instead of exercising the Trial Spawner sound and subtitle event described by the formal reproduction steps.
